title: Rene Jelpie and Monk Smith's guitar styles
summary: Rene picked self-taught fingerstyle melody and variations, while Monk strummed chords; the interviewer compares this to the early records.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I remember when Rene Jalpe played, how did he work it? Did he strum chords or did he pick with his fingers?
Do you remember? He picked with his fingers.
So he would be playing something that was pretty complex.

He would be playing the melody and variations on the melody and everything else. He played it like nobody ever heard before. I agree. And he taught himself. I mean I don't think he ever had a lesson in his life. But he picked it up somewhere along the line and he played it extremely well.
And Monk Smith, did he play fingerstyle or strumming?
When he played he was strumming. He had a great big old guitar and he was just playing chords strumming.

That works out very well with the lower register clarinet that Pinky used to play on the records. You have to hear all those records. Those records are still great. When they go back to the two string instruments you can get some feeling of what the Invincibles and the old 6 and 7 8s must have sounded like. But they'd never been a violin on those records.
